_comment: Status line for each interactive page (src/components/PageStatus.astro). `checked` repeats, in short, the validation the page itself states, with the tools/ directory that checks it; change both together. `basedOn` lists the paper (ADS bibcode) and notebook or code the page adapts. `files` are the paths whose latest commit gives the 'Updated' date. To add a page, add an entry keyed by its path and put <PageStatus page="..." /> at the end of its hero. Every entry is also listed on /explore/ (src/lib/interactive.ts): optional `explore` sets its title, one-line teaser, area (solar-system | detection | exoplanets | moons | software), `featured` (an order number: shown on the homepage strip) and `visual` (a thumbnail kind in src/components/ExploreThumb.astro); without it the title, summary and area come from the tutorial or software record whose `interactive` points to the page.

explore.title: How do you find an orbit?
explore.teaser: From the first night's observations of 2024 YR4 to its orbit, with every calculation running in your browser.

teaching/orbit-determination.checked: Started from JPL's orbit, matches JPL Horizons for all 409 observations to 0.021″; Gauss's method and the least-squares fits agree with an independent Python reference.

teaching/asteroid-belt.checked: The Kepler solver agrees with REBOUND's two-body integration to within 40 km for 400 sampled orbits over ±50 years.

explore.title: Same orbit. Different point of view.
explore.teaser: Kamoʻoalewa, Hektor and Hilda from one N-body integration, drawn in five reference frames.

teaching/reference-frames.checked: Agrees with REBOUND's IAS15 integrator to within 35 km for Earth–Kamoʻoalewa, and 50 m for Jupiter–Hektor and Jupiter–Hilda, over 400 years.

explore.title: When do close planets become chaotic?
explore.teaser: Map where neighbouring resonances overlap and pairs of close planets become chaotic.

teaching/resonance-overlap.checked: Agrees with the notebook on whether an orbit is chaotic for 747 of 750 test pixels; the other three lie on the boundary.

explore.title: Can a planet hide from transit timing?
explore.teaser: How inclined and retrograde companions change the timing of a planet's transits.

teaching/transit-timing.checked: RMS TTVs agree with the notebook's REBOUND (IAS15) runs to about one part in ten thousand (median) over 64 systems.

explore.title: Linking asteroids by guessing their distance
explore.teaser: Link tracklets from different nights by guessing each asteroid's distance from the Sun, as in HelioLinC.

teaching/heliolinc.checked: Finds exactly the same numbers of pure, valid and erroneous clusters as the notebook in seven of seven tests.

explore.title: Which interstellar visitors will Rubin see?
explore.teaser: Where in the sky, and how often, the Rubin Observatory's survey should find interstellar objects.

teaching/interstellar-objects.checked: Positions agree with the notebook to 10⁻¹¹ au for 57 objects, and visibility on all 62,472 nights.

explore.title: Fitting planets that pull on each other
explore.teaser: Fit radial velocities with full N-body models of interacting planets.

teaching/run-dmc.checked: The N-body model agrees with the notebook's REBOUND model to 0.02 m/s, and the log posterior near the best fit to 0.015.

explore.title: Three planets in step: the Laplace resonance of GJ 876
explore.teaser: Follow the resonant angles of three planets locked together around the star GJ 876.

teaching/laplace-resonance.checked: Agrees with REBOUND's IAS15 on the star's radial velocity to 10⁻⁴ m/s over 200 days, and on every libration amplitude to within 0.1°.

explore.title: Finding moving objects hidden in the noise
explore.teaser: Recover objects too faint to detect on any one night by stacking detections along trial motions.

teaching/shift-and-stack.checked: Gives exactly the same clusters as the notebook on the same catalogue.

explore.title: How do planets lose their moons around white dwarfs?
explore.teaser: As a dying star loses mass, its planets' orbits widen and their moons can be set free.

teaching/exomoons.checked: For 160 test moons, agrees with REBOUND on the fate of all 159 that the page can follow.

explore.title: Could Cassini have felt Planet Nine?
explore.teaser: Would a distant planet's tidal pull on Saturn show up in the Cassini ranging data?

teaching/cassini-planet-nine.checked: Matches the notebook's results to better than 10⁻⁶.

explore.title: What’s in an orbit file?
explore.teaser: Explore the fields of an MPC orbit in the mpc_orb JSON format.

software/mpc-orb.checked: Two-body motion agrees with REBOUND to under a metre over 50 years. Not an ephemeris.

explore.title: Where is the observatory?
explore.teaser: Find where an observatory was, on the ground or in space, from its MPC code.

software/wis.checked: Observatory positions agree with wis to within about 200 m from 2000 to 2026; spacecraft positions to within 500 m.
